title: SSH Terrapin prefix truncation weakness on production physical hosts

case_origin.source: Tenable vulnerability export supplied for thesis experiment

experimental_selection_reason: Medium-severity SSH protocol weakness affecting two critical production hosts; selected to test nuanced assessment of a conditional man-in-the-middle attack.

finding.synopsis: The remote SSH server is vulnerable to a man-in-the-middle prefix truncation attack.
finding.description:
The remote SSH server is vulnerable to a man-in-the-middle prefix truncation weakness known as Terrapin. This can allow a remote, man-in-the-middle attacker to bypass integrity checks and downgrade the connection's security.

Note that this plugin only checks for remote SSH servers that support either ChaCha20-Poly1305 or CBC with Encrypt-then-MAC and do not support the strict key exchange countermeasures. It does not check for vulnerable software versions.
finding.recommended_remediation: Contact the vendor for an update with the strict key exchange countermeasures or disable the affected algorithms.
